questions.stem: The Natyashastra, the foundational Sanskrit treatise on Indian classical dance, drama, and music, was authored by which ancient sage?

options.option_text: Abhinavagupta, the Kashmir Shaivite philosopher
Bharata Muni, the ancient musicologist and dramatist
Patanjali, compiler of the Yoga Sutras of India
Vishnu Sharma, the author of Panchatantra fables

questions.explanation: B is correct because Bharata Muni authored the Natyashastra (circa 200 BCE–200 CE), the encyclopaedic treatise on performance arts that defines rasa, bhava, abhinaya, and stage rules still followed today. Abhinavagupta (Option A) is a common trap — he wrote Abhinavabharati, a 10th-century commentary ON the Natyashastra, but did not author it.

questions.stem: In Indian classical dance theory, TANDAVA is the vigorous, masculine style of movement. Which iconic form of Lord Shiva performing Tandava is depicted in the famous Chola bronze sculptures?

options.option_text: Ardhanarishvara — the androgynous half-Shiva form
Nataraja — Shiva as the cosmic Lord of Dance
Dakshinamurti — Shiva as the silent teacher-guru
Bhairava — the fierce, destructive form of Shiva

questions.explanation: B is correct. Nataraja (Raja of Nata = dance) shows Shiva performing the Ananda Tandava within a ring of fire (Prabhamandala), trampling Apasmara (ignorance) underfoot. The Chola bronzes from Tamil Nadu are world-famous representations. Bhairava (Option D) is a common distractor as it is Shiva's fearsome form, but it is not associated with the cosmic dance iconography.

questions.stem: Chhau dance is practised in three distinct regional styles across eastern India. Which of the following CORRECTLY pairs all three Chhau variants with their respective states?

options.option_text: Purulia→Odisha; Seraikella→West Bengal; Mayurbhanj→Jharkhand
Purulia→West Bengal; Seraikella→Jharkhand; Mayurbhanj→Odisha
Purulia→Jharkhand; Seraikella→Odisha; Mayurbhanj→West Bengal
Purulia→West Bengal; Seraikella→Odisha; Mayurbhanj→Jharkhand

questions.explanation: B is correct. Purulia Chhau belongs to West Bengal, Seraikella Chhau to Jharkhand (formerly part of Bihar), and Mayurbhanj Chhau to Odisha. A key distinction: Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed WITHOUT masks, while Purulia and Seraikella styles use elaborate painted masks. UNESCO inscribed Chhau on the Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010. Option A is the most common wrong answer as it swaps Purulia and Seraikella.

questions.stem: The Abhinaya Darpana ('Mirror of Gesture'), a classical manual describing hand gestures (mudras) and facial expressions used in Indian dance, is attributed to which author?

options.option_text: Bharata Muni, who also composed the Natyashastra
Nandikeshvara, a sage in the ancient Shaiva tradition
Rukmini Devi Arundale, reformer of Bharatanatyam
Jayadeva, the poet who wrote Gita Govinda verses

questions.explanation: B is correct. Nandikeshvara authored the Abhinaya Darpana, which details the 28 Asamyuta (single-hand) and 24 Samyuta (combined) hastas that form the gestural vocabulary of Bharatanatyam and Odissi. Bharata Muni (Option A) is the most tempting distractor since his Natyashastra also covers abhinaya, but the Abhinaya Darpana is a separate, later text specifically attributed to Nandikeshvara.

questions.stem: In the traditional Bharatanatyam Margam (recital sequence), which dance item functions as the grand finale — characterised by fast rhythmic syllables (jatis), vigorous footwork, and abstract nritta?

options.option_text: Varnam — the lengthiest, central piece combining nritta and abhinaya
Thillana — the fast-paced concluding item built on rhythmic patterns
Shabdam — a devotional piece with narrative lyrical content
Jatiswaram — rhythmic-melodic composition without textual lyrics

questions.explanation: B is correct. The standard Margam sequence runs: Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam/Keertanam → Thillana → Mangalam. Thillana is the penultimate item and the energetic showpiece finale before the closing Mangalam benediction. Varnam (Option A) is the longest and technically most demanding piece but appears in the middle of the recital, not at the end.

questions.stem: In Manipuri classical dance, the performance form 'Pung Cholom' takes its name from the 'Pung'. What exactly is the Pung?

options.option_text: The double-headed barrel drum central to Manipuri music
The wide cylindrical skirt worn by female Ras Lila dancers
A devotional composition in the Meitei language of Manipur
The arched jewelled headdress worn in Lai Haraoba ceremonies

questions.explanation: A is correct. Pung (also called Mridang Manipuri or Dholak Manipuri) is the distinctive two-faced barrel drum of Manipur. Pung Cholom is a dance-percussion form where male performers play the Pung while executing acrobatic leaps and turns — the drum is an active prop, not just accompaniment. Option B (the skirt) refers to the Potloi, the stiff, cylindrical costume worn by female dancers in Ras Lila. Pung should not be confused with Kartal (cymbals) which also feature prominently in Manipuri recitals.

questions.stem: The Bombay Devadasi Protection Act (1934) was the first Indian law to formally prohibit the dedication of women to temples as Devadasis. However, the practice of dance these women performed — once called 'Sadir' — was revived as a respectable classical art form largely through the efforts of which institution?

options.option_text: Kalakshetra Foundation, established by Rukmini Devi Arundale in 1936
Sangeet Natak Akademi, established by the Government of India in 1952
Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, founded by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar in 1901
Bhatkhande Music Institute, established in Lucknow in 1926

questions.explanation: A is correct. Rukmini Devi Arundale founded Kalakshetra ('sacred ground of arts') in Adyar, Chennai in 1936, where she systematically de-stigmatised Sadir and renamed it Bharatanatyam, establishing notation, costuming, and pedagogical standards still followed globally. The Sangeet Natak Akademi (Option B) is a frequent distractor as it recognises classical forms officially, but it was founded in 1952 — after the revival was already well underway — and is a recognition body, not a revival institution.
